_about: Scripted customers at the counter (CounterRules.scripted). 'schedule' books them by chapter and day (days count from Monday 7 October 2019 = 0). A story step can also bring its own: { "type": "counter", "day": 9, "customers": ["dale_hatch", { ...a spec... }] }. Keys: kind (story or familia), cast (a StoryScript.CAST face), person, car (catalogue id, paint), request, problem (a CounterRules problem id, or clean), excuse (a covered discrepancy with valid proof), papers (overrides per document: reg, licence, insurance, sheet, work, invoice; reg.use and sheet.tires from week 8), says, napkin, mask, letter ({title, lines}), ask (topic -> {line, doc, clue}), clue ({id, note}: what Leo can write in his notebook from what they say), outcomes (stamp -> {line, citation, money, dirty, heat, trust, review, correct, flags}), arrive (H:MM), forged (their proof is a bad one), from_away (the car came from another province), seed (instead of the id), quiet (no desk_<id>_<stamp> flag). 'regulars' (DeskRegulars) are the people who keep coming back: person, car, ask (small talk), and visits [{day, ...the same keys..., after_id, after: {last stamp -> what changes}}]. The last stamp is APPROVED, DENIED, REPORT or WRENCH (with _WRONG when it was the wrong call; the plain key covers both) or WALKED; a branch with a problem brings its own papers and lines; hello goes in front of says.

dale_hatch.says: MY GUYS ARE SWAMPED, SO HERE I AM. SAFETY ON THIS ONE, SON. FRANKIE ALWAYS DID MY USED ONES.

letter.title: HATCH MOTORS
lines: FROM THE DESK OF DALE HATCH
A FAIR PRICE. FOR FRANK'S KIDS.

local.line: THE MOUNTAIN TIM BURTONS. FRANKIE AND I USED TO SIT IN THAT LOT. HE TOOK IT BLACK. CHECKED HIS BRAKES EVERY SUNDAY, TOO. CAREFUL MAN.

clue.note: HATCH KNOWS DAD CHECKED HIS BRAKES EVERY SUNDAY. SO DID EVERYBODY, I GUESS.

APPROVED.line: "Good man. Frankie's boy." He tucks the card under the mug. "Think about it. For Aries." You never told him her name.

DENIED.line: He laughs like it's a joke you both told. "Sure, son. Sure." There was nothing wrong with it. He knows you know.

REPORT.line: Constable Tremblay looks at the papers, looks at Hatch, and buys him a coffee. Then she looks at you for a long time.

WRENCH.line: "Off the books? Son, I sell cars. Everything I do is on the books." He smiles. Gus puts his coffee down.
